summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — APP +30%, CPAY +8%, CF +6%, VRSK +4%, MSI +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (SNDK -21%, WDC -17%, P -16%, MU -16%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: APP (+29.95%) — Likely a post-Q3 earnings reaction: AppLovin reported revenue of $2.18B (+55% y/y) and EPS of $4.30 versus about $3.95 expected. I couldn't find a source tying the +29.95% move to today. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: APP is a large-cap ad-tech/software name that no strategy includes. Earnings-driven gaps also happen at the open, so a momentum or mean-reversion filter would see the move only after the gap.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely a post-Q3 earnings reaction: AppLovin reported revenue of $2.18B (+55% y/y) and EPS of $4.30 versus about $3.95 expected. I couldn't find a source tying the +29.95% move to today.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: APP is a large-cap ad-tech/software name that no strategy includes. Earnings-driven gaps also happen at the open, so a momentum or mean-reversion filter would see the move only after the gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta large-cap names like APP to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings gate release names that gap up 15% or more on a beat, once volume in the first 30 minutes is at least 2x average.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely post-Q3 earnings follow-through: results out Nov 4 beat guidance (adj. EPS $7.54 vs ~$7.05-7.25 guided, revenue +18%). I found no same-day Nov 6 article, so this driver is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CPAY is a roughly $30B mid/large-cap fintech/payments name that no strategy lists. The catalyst also came two sessions earlier, so an earnings-gated or gap-up filter would have had no fresh signal on Nov 6.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drift screen over a broad mid-cap universe: admit names with an earnings beat in the last 3 sessions and a close-to-close gain ≥ +5% on above-average volume, rather than only same-day gaps.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found. Likely a delayed reaction to Q3 results (reported after the close Nov 4), plus a nitrogen/urea price rally tied to Hormuz-related supply fears.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CF is a mid-cap fertilizer/basic-materials name, and no strategy covers it. A post-earnings and commodity-driven move would also have been missed by technical filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a commodity-chemicals/fertilizer sector basket (CF, NTR, MOS, LXU) to the momentum universe and relax the earnings-gate to release names with a post-results gap or follow-through of ≥+3% on day 2.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely a rebound after the Nov 5 Q3 selloff (revenue $809M, reportedly a miss vs. estimates; guidance maintained). No fresh Nov 6 news found, so this is inferred, not confirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: VRSK is a mid/large-cap data-analytics name that no strategy includes. A bounce after an earnings-driven drop is also a mean-reversion move that momentum and news-reactive filters would skip.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drop rebound screen to the mean-reversion universe: admit S&P 500 names that fell ≥5% on an earnings day and close ≥+3% the next session on volume ≥1.2× the 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely a reaction to Motorola Solutions' Q3 2026 results (record backlog ~$16.6B, +14% y/y, per its 8-K). I couldn't confirm today's price reaction or any guidance raise, so the cause is unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MSI is a ~$85B large-cap in communications and public-safety tech. If earnings drove the move, the gap came at the open, so a post-open momentum filter would see it as too late or too extended.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap (>$50B) names to the universe of the earnings-gap strategy, and release the earnings-gate for gaps of +3% or more with volume above 1.5x the 20-day average within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news. Likely a delayed rebound after the weak Q3 print (~Nov 3-4: net loss $72M, phosphate loss, sulfur-constrained output) and a sector bounce in fertilizer/potash.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MOS is a mid-cap fertilizer/materials name that no strategy lists. The move also had no clear catalyst, so a news-reactive filter would have nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-momentum scan that lets mid-cap materials/ag names enter a momentum universe when price is up 3% or more on volume of at least 1.5× the 20-day average. Cap it at a small position size.

top_movers.catalyst: No same-day news found for Nov 6. Likely continued AI-memory/NAND unwind after the Oct 30 -13.5% drop on Kioxia's outlook that flash price strength is fading, plus pre-split (8-for-1, Nov 20) volatility.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SNDK is a ~$120B+ memory/NAND name with a ~$800+ share price that no strategy lists. It was also a sector-driven move with no clear catalyst, so news-reactive filters had nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta AI-semis/memory names (SNDK, MU, WDC) to the mean-reversion universe, with a sector-drawdown trigger such as 5-day move ≤ -25% and a price-cap check that allows ~$800+ share prices.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide memory/storage rout (SanDisk, Micron, Seagate also down sharply) on post-midterm AI-bubble worries, AI-pause rhetoric and supply-glut fears; no WDC-specific news found. Some dating is uncertain.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: WDC is a large-cap hardware/storage name that no strategy's universe includes. The bot also seems to be long-only, so it could not short a macro/sector-driven drop.
top_movers.suggestion: Add memory/storage names (WDC, STX, SNDK, MU) to a sector-momentum universe with a 'sector_drawdown' gate: flag a basket drop of ≥8% in one session as a risk-off signal that trims exposure to correlated AI/semis holdings.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found — searches returned nothing for P on 2026-11-06 (ticker is ambiguous). A -16% single-day drop on a ~$94 stock is consistent with an earnings or guidance shock, but that is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe, probably a mid-cap name that fails the universe's cap, liquidity or sector screens. If it was an earnings gap-down, the bot has no short capability, and long-only momentum and mean-reversion filters would not enter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a universe-audit log that records top losers/gainers (|move| ≥ 10%) missing from every strategy universe, with market cap and ADV, so the market-cap/ADV floor can be tuned from data. Resolve ambiguous single-letter tickers by company name.

top_movers.catalyst: Memory-chip selloff deepened: fears of Chinese competition (CXMT) and a 2029 DRAM oversupply, plus hot inflation prints and rate-hike worries, hit MU, SanDisk and SK Hynix. No MU-specific news was found.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MU is a large-cap semiconductor name that no strategy includes, and this was a sector-wide, multi-day drawdown with no single catalyst for a news-reactive bot to key on. The bot is also likely long-only, so it can't short.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-breadth rule: when ≥3 names in a semiconductor/memory basket fall >8% in a day, flag a risk-off regime and cut long exposure in correlated holdings. Alternatively, add MU to a mean-reversion universe with an RSI<25 filter.
